behaviors.protocol_context: Fixed replica set; instance identified by origin replica and instance number; per-instance ballot
writes: Owner batches requests and allocates an instance in its row. startPhase1 computes key-indexed dependencies and installs PREACCEPTED plus fresh bookkeeping.
Follower rejects lower ballots; for status below ACCEPTED it records commands, updated attributes, ballot/value ballot and PREACCEPTED or PREACCEPTED_EQ.
Replies matching lastTriedBallot and a preaccepted bookkeeping status increment support and merge attributes; higher value ballots replace selected attributes/status.
important_branches: Fast decision requires FastQuorumSize()-1 replies, allEqual, committed-dependency condition for N>7, and initial ballot. Equality is skipped for N<=3 with thriftiness.
At the same threshold without fast precondition, coordinator installs ACCEPTED and broadcasts Accept.
For existing ACCEPTED-or-later state, PreAccept only fills missing commands; it indexes the command write by LeaderId, while reading the instance by Replica.
external_effects: Conditional metadata/command persistence and sync, PreAccept replies, Accept or Commit broadcasts, early client replies only if Dreply is false.

behaviors.protocol_context: Fixed replica set; instance identified by origin replica and instance number; per-instance ballot
implementation_guards: Follower rejects lower ballots and does not alter COMMITTED/EXECUTED records.
Coordinator requires bookkeeping ACCEPTED and reply ballot exactly lastTriedBallot.
writes: For an eligible Accept, follower assigns Deps, Seq, bal and vbal but leaves Status unchanged.
Coordinator increments acceptOKs; acceptOKs+1>N/2 sets bookkeeping and instance COMMITTED.
external_effects: Follower records metadata, syncs and replies with its current ballot. Coordinator commits, propagates and conditionally replies to clients.
unknowns: Does preservation of an acknowledged Accept require an ACCEPTED status visible to subsequent Prepare and PreAccept processing?

behaviors.protocol_context: Fixed replica set; instance identified by origin replica and instance number; per-instance ballot
writes: Recovery retains pending client proposals, snapshots current value information into new bookkeeping, selects ballot and appends a self PrepareReply after overwriting local bal and vbal.
Prepare raises bal for a higher request, retaining vbal and value/status, then replies.

Matching prepare replies accumulate until SlowQuorumSize. Highest VBallot with last-on-tie selection supplies value/status. Recovery branches on COMMITTED, ACCEPTED, or preaccepted counts/equality/leader participation; otherwise restarts phase1, using NOOP for absent commands.
important_branches: Complete committed commands suppress recovery initiation. Selected committed state is installed without a Commit broadcast in this handler.
Old or mismatching prepare replies are rejected by preparing/ballot checks. New recovery bookkeeping resets old counters.
makeBallot uses replica identity, N, and only when IsLeader is true advances against maxRecvBallot. BeTheLeader sets IsLeader true; no revocation is shown.

facts.meaning: The local instance record carries its current command/attribute tuple, status, promise ballot and value ballot; these fields are what Prepare exports and formation/execution interprets. This does not assert that every acknowledgement establishes ACCEPTED or that the tuple is chosen.
facts.validity_context: In-memory snapshot at a serialized handler boundary; later protocol handlers may replace fields. Execution concurrently consumes and marks records.
facts.durability: Conditional helpers exist; launcher disables Durable. No crash-restart claim established.
facts.recovery: PrepareReply exports this tuple; recovery selects by VBallot and uses status to choose continuation.
unknowns: Whether follower Accept acknowledgement preserves the support classification needed across recovery.

formation.explanation: A1: A client proposal is batched by its receiving replica into a local-row instance. Conflict indexes supply sequence/dependencies; thriftiness selects a preferred live peer subset. PreAccept replies are filtered by attempted ballot and phase, then counted/merged. Fast conditions commit directly; otherwise Accept replies at matching ballot establish the coordinator commit threshold. Commit broadcasts carry commands and attributes. Recipients install guarded committed records. Dependency/SCC execution waits for prerequisite commands and committed status, applies ordered operations and answers deferred clients.

context.explanation: A2: Authority is per instance, not exclusive global proposal leadership. Initial ballots equal origin replica ID. Recovery resets bookkeeping while retaining client proposals/value context, selects a ballot, adds a self reply and sends Prepare. Acceptors raise their promise and export prior value ballot/status. The recovering coordinator collects matching replies and selects a highest-value-ballot tuple before committing locally, accepting or restarting phase1. Lower-ballot requests and nonmatching replies are guarded. Complete committed records skip recovery. Master designation affects higher-ballot retry but does not stop other replicas proposing.

connection.explanation: A1/A2 connection: The record status and value ballot exported by Prepare determine whether earlier formation support constrains the new attempt as committed, accepted or merely preaccepted. Reset bookkeeping discards old counts; phase and ballot checks constrain delayed replies. Accepted/committed follower guards limit new PreAccept modifications, while delayed Commit is rejected below a newer promise. Pending local client proposals survive recovery and may be reproposed after NOOP. Execution later consumes the selected record, so retention of support classification matters independently of client visibility.

open_details: Follower Accept leaves Status unchanged; investigate preservation through Prepare.
Prepare selection overwrites equal-VBallot tuples in reply order; recoverer also rewrites self vbal before exporting it.
TryPreAccept recovery subcase has duplicate condition after the prior branch; deeper reachability remains open.
Transport queues per message asynchronously; legal dispatch histories and shared-memory observations need question-specific review.
Fault/restart and client retry contracts remain incomplete.
